right-mindfulness.affirm: Gunaratana (Mindfulness in Plain English, via Bodhi's paper)
right-mindfulness.verdict: PASS — direct affirm/deny on whether sati is by nature non-conceptual; Bodhi explicitly denies the claim Gunaratana affirms.

right-mindfulness.q: Is sati awareness of the present moment, or remembering?
right-mindfulness.verdict: UNRESOLVED on the strict same-conditions test — the two definitions give opposite answers on sati's core (present-moment attending vs retention), but the dossier itself notes Kabat-Zinn's 2011 reply that his was an operational definition for a clinical setting and that whether one capacity or two is left open by the sources; whether the authors exclude each other's account WITHIN THE SAME SETTING is not established by the opened passages. Recorded as a live definitional dispute, not a certified head-on denial.

Recorded as a live dispute with the qualification preserved.

right-view.q: Is the person known as a real and ultimate fact?

right-view.verdict: PASS — opposite verdicts; dossier notes the sutta's own test does not settle which side.

freedom.q: Is the liberty that binds still liberty?
freedom.verdict: PASS — Constant explicitly reads Rousseau's transposition as furnishing 'deadly pretexts for more than one kind of tyranny'.

freedom.q: Is choice an explanatory starting point?
freedom.deny: Skinner (Beyond Freedom and Dignity, CUP excerpt)
freedom.verdict: PASS — Skinner rejects the autonomous chooser as explanatory; dossier notes the causal question stays open (not a dissolution of the propositions).

freedom.q: Is the other's freedom a threat or the medium of mine?
freedom.verdict: PASS with qualification — dossier itself cites Kirkpatrick's caution that reading Beauvoir vs Sartre as disagreeing remains disputable; recorded as a live interpretive dispute, not a settled head-on denial.

freedom.q: Does a free act have to escape the causal chain?
freedom.verdict: PASS — Kant calls the comparative notion 'a wretched subterfuge'; the pairing is the dossier's own (Kant does not name Hume), honestly flagged.

right-concentration.q: Is the collected mind fixed on one point or gathered into a whole field?
right-concentration.affirm: Buddhaghosa one-pointedness (Visuddhimagga, via Wikipedia Samadhi, checked against raw HTML)
right-concentration.verdict: PASS — the dossier notes the article's Criticism section reports the one-pointed interpretation 'has become a matter of debate'; live dispute.

right-concentration.q: Does the mind fade with use, or drift from boredom?
right-concentration.affirm_depletion: resource-depletion account (as reported in Langner & Eickhoff 2013)
right-concentration.verdict: PASS with qualification — a genuine live empirical dispute between two accounts, but the review itself takes no side (neither account consistent with all data); recorded as unresolved-in-the-sources rather than a head-on affirm/deny between two named authors.

right-concentration.q: Is concentration for stilling the mind or for seeing what it does?
right-concentration.deny: SN 22.5 (Sujato trans.) — immersion for knowing arising and ending
right-concentration.verdict: UNRESOLVED on the strict test — Patanjali's endpoint (the seer abiding in his own nature) and SN 22.5's endpoint (knowledge of arising and ending) are different aims, but the dossier itself warns the contrast may be sharper than the full Yoga text supports (discernment appears as a stage in I.17) and neither quoted passage establishes that the two endpoints cannot coexist in one practitioner. Recorded as an open comparison, not a certified head-on denial.

right-concentration.affirm: Gunaratana (The Jhanas in Theravada Buddhist Meditation; Visuddhimagga dry-insight admission)
right-concentration.deny: Thanissaro (SN 12.70 note; Wings to Awakening part 3)
right-concentration.verdict: PASS — opposite answers on whether awakening requires the absorptions; dossier notes part of the gap is term scope (mundane vs supramundane jhana).
